chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abdullah al-Kinanī, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who entered into iḥram but forgot to trim his nails. He said: 'He leaves them.' I said: 'Even if they are long?' He said: 'Even if they are.' I said: 'Indeed, a man gave him a fatwa to trim them, take a bath (ghusl), and renew his iḥram, so he did.' He said: 'Upon him is a dam (blood sacrifice).'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.دَم: Blood sacrifice, a specific expiation offering in Hajj
key_terms.يُقَلِّمَ: To trim or cut (specifically nails or hair)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets to trim their nails while in iḥram?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the scholar distinguishes between the prohibition of cutting nails and the penalty incurred for doing so, emphasizing that mere length does not mandate immediate removal. The ruling highlights the principle of 'dam' (a specific sacrificial offering) as the expiation for violating the state of iḥram through this specific act, reflecting the Shia juristic view on minor violations during pilgrimage. This serves as a practical guide for pilgrims to maintain ritual purity without incurring unnecessary penalties for forgetfulness or minor oversights.
